page: Amazon Web Services m8id.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, powered by a 32-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core and incorporates an extensive 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 and AMX acceleration. The server features 256 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 7 GHz, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Unlike standard diskless instances, it includes 3,800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 30 Gbps baseline network interface without discrete graphics processing hardware.

Performance testing reflects high multi-core throughput and strong data-processing efficiency. The processor achieves top-tier scores in multi-core Geekbench assessments and Clang software compilation, alongside upper-quartile PassMark compute and stress-ng results. In-memory and cache pipelines demonstrate strong bandwidth, measuring over 5,100 GB/s on small-block cached read benchmarks and sustaining 112.74 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance also registers top-decile marks in static web serving throughput and large language model prompt evaluation.

Integrating 3,800 GB of local NVMe storage delivers high IOPS and low-latency storage access without requiring dedicated external block storage volume overhead. However, workloads utilizing this instance store must account for the ephemeral nature of local drives through replication or external backups. The combination of dense DDR5 memory, fast local storage, and 64 compute threads makes the server well aligned for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, continuous integration build clusters, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.16xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-virtualized instance equipped with a 32-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs at 3.9 GHz and a 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 256 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 30 Gbps baseline networking. Compute benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded performance in software compilation, web serving throughput, and large model prompt processing, bolstered by AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions. Memory and cache tests exhibit strong data throughput, handling over 112 million Redis operations per second. While the bundled local storage provides low-latency disk IO without external block attachment overhead, it requires application-level persistence management. The instance is well matched for high-throughput relational databases, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD build environments, and enterprise web applications.
